institution: McGill University — Schulich School of Music
accreditationStatus: Public research university, degree-granting under Quebec provincial charter; U15 member
durationEcts: 2 years full-time; 48 McGill credits (15 credits graduate seminars + 33 credits thesis research). No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: Research-based thesis degree inside the Music Technology Area / CIRMMT: music information retrieval, digital audio signal processing, sound synthesis, audio recording and production, music perception and cognition, gestural control and new interfaces for musical expression (NIME), spatial audio, acoustics. Strong engineering/science orientation rather than artist-portfolio orientation.
entryRequirements: "A bachelor's degree in Music Technology or a related scientific or technological field (engineering, computer science, psychology, physics, etc.) from a university recognized by McGill"; minimum CGPA 3.0/4.0 (or 3.2/4.0 in the last two years of full-time study). Applicants must "demonstrate evidence of expertise in music technology". Identifying/being accepted by a supervisor among the Music Technology faculty is effectively required.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Programme page: "Students are accepted from a wide range of musical backgrounds and have solid training in math, computer science, acoustics, and experimental psychology." Admissions page lists "a bachelor's degree in Music Technology or a related scientific or technological field (engineering, computer science, psychology, physics, etc.)". A BSc Software Engineering is squarely inside the accepted background. NOTE: the page also warns that "Applicants with limited Music Technology backgrounds or CGPA below 3.0 may be considered as undergraduate 'special' students to take preparatory courses, then reapply to the M.A. program" — i.e. a candidate with zero music-technology evidence risks being routed to a qualifying year first.
portfolioSpec: Work samples in music technology are required: "Work samples in music technology must be submitted" (mt.music.mcgill.ca/programmes_and_admissions). The page does not fix a number or duration of items — it is a research/work-sample portfolio (code, research reports, audio/DSP projects, papers), NOT a conservatoire creative portfolio. Exact item count/format: UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: No live audition. The M.A. Music Technology is a research degree admitted on file (transcripts, statement, references, work samples). Unlike McGill's performance/composition M.Mus. degrees there is no audition requirement stated anywhere on the Music Technology admissions pages.
tuitionNonEU: CAD 10,674.30 per year (2026-27 full-time international thesis-residency master's flat rate, McGill Student Accounts). Thesis students are billed a flat per-term rate, not per credit.
otherFees: Compulsory student-society, registration, IT and service fees plus mandatory international health insurance (McGill Blue Cross / RVSQ), typically CAD 2,500–4,500/yr combined. Application fee CAD ~135. Exact 2027-28 figures: UNVERIFIED.
totalCostEstimate: Tuition + fees roughly CAD 14,000–15,500/yr; Montreal living costs roughly CAD 15,000–18,000/yr. Two-year total order of magnitude CAD 58,000–67,000 before any funding. With an RA from a supervisor's grant plus a differential fee waiver, net cost can fall dramatically.
scholarshipName: McGill differential fee waiver; supervisor-funded Research Assistantships; CIRMMT Student Awards; Graduate Excellence Fellowships
scholarships: REAL BUT CONDITIONAL FUNDING ROUTE. (1) Differential fee waiver: "McGill offers a limited number of one-year differential fee waivers (exemptions from the international tuition supplement) to international students" — reduces tuition toward the Quebec/Canadian rate; nomination is by the department, no separate application; covers tuition supplement only, not living. (2) Internal funding: McGill states "not all master's students receive internal funding" and the range offered is roughly CAD 1,000–24,000 spread over 2 years — at the top end this covers tuition and a large share of living. (3) The decisive route is a Research Assistantship paid from a supervisor's grant (NSERC/FRQNT/SSHRC/CIRMMT); the department lists "Research Assistantships (supported by supervisor)" among the sources its students actually use. Tunisians ARE eligible for all of these — they are internal/departmental, not citizenship-restricted. (4) Vanier CGS is DOCTORAL ONLY, so it does not apply to this M.A. (5) There is no guaranteed funding package: an unfunded admit is unaffordable. Deadline for internal award consideration = the December 1 application deadline (single application, no separate award form).
languageRequirement: English. Tunisian applicant educated in Arabic/French must submit a test.
englishTest: IELTS Academic band 6.5 overall minimum (McGill graduate minimum); TOEFL iBT minimum for graduate studies is 86 overall with no component below 20 (McGill graduate standard). Programme may demand higher. GRE: not required for M.A. Music Technology (no GRE requirement stated on Music Technology admission pages).
deadline: December 1 for the following September (Fall) intake — so 1 December 2026 for September 2027 entry. This is AFTER September 2026, i.e. still open to him.
applicationOpens: September 15 (McGill uApply opens 15 September for the following Fall; McGill Music separately lists October 1 for its graduate music applications — treat 15 September 2026 as the earliest opening for the 2027 cycle).
_verdict: STRONG TECHNICAL FIT, WEAK ARTIST FIT. His BSc Software Engineering is exactly the background McGill wants and Canadian tuition is low by Anglophone standards. But this is a research degree that produces a thesis, not an electronic-music artist. And with no portfolio at all he cannot 'demonstrate evidence of expertise in music technology' — he must build a body of DSP/audio-code/production work during 2026 to be admissible at all. Affordability hinges entirely on landing a supervisor with grant money.

institution: Université de Montréal — Faculté de musique
program: Maîtrise en musique, option Composition et création sonore
accreditationStatus: Public university, Quebec provincial charter; degree recognised across Canada
language: FRENCH (entirely). Letter of intent must be written in French.
durationEcts: 45 UdeM credits, full-time, normally 2 years (research/creation pathway with mémoire or travail dirigé). No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: Per the Faculté de musique: instrumental and vocal composition, mixed composition, ELECTROACOUSTIC AND ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION, performing arts and sound installations, media arts, and software arts applied to sound and musical creation. Seminars in musical technologies: computer-assisted composition, digital lutherie and interactive systems, audio effects. UdeM also runs the 'musiques numériques' stream and hosts a strong electroacoustic tradition (Montreal is the world centre of acousmatic music).
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) with adequate standing; admission is CONDITIONAL on securing a faculty supervisor willing to direct the research-creation. Portfolio and a French-language letter of intent are mandatory for the file to be examined.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIAL / NOT EXPLICITLY. The programme does not publish a blanket 'any bachelor's' clause; it is a music master's whose gate is the portfolio and the supervisor's willingness. A non-music bachelor is not disqualified in the published rules, but the applicant must demonstrate compositional/sound-creation ability through the 2-5 work portfolio and may be required to complete a 'propédeutique' (qualifying year) — a standard Quebec mechanism. NOT VERIFIED as an explicit written allowance; treat as portfolio-gated rather than degree-gated.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: "deux (2) à cinq (5) oeuvres ou réalisations en composition et/ou création sonore" representative of the applicant's artistic approach. Plus: a curriculum vitae; a MANDATORY two-page letter of intent WRITTEN IN FRENCH sketching the research-creation project, prior background, training projects and professional objectives; and two academic works — one written (history / programme notes) and one analytical (formal, harmonic).
auditionSpec: No live performance audition for the composition option. NOTE: an 'audition/examination' administrative fee of minimum CAD 53.50 (non-refundable, charged once) is levied on the application — this is a file-examination fee, not evidence of a live audition. Some UdeM music options do require in-person or recorded auditions; Composition et création sonore is assessed on the submitted portfolio.
tuitionNonEU: CAD 11,375.92 per semester for international students, full-time 15 credits (2025-26 published rate) = CAD 22,751.84 for a 30-credit year; ≈ CAD 758.39 per credit; ≈ CAD 34,128 for the full 45 credits BEFORE the automatic exemption bursary.
otherFees: CAD 1,000 deposit required from international applicants after acceptance (credited toward tuition). Compulsory student and service fees plus mandatory health insurance. Indexation for international graduate research students is 3%/yr.
totalCostEstimate: AFTER the automatic UdeM exemption bursary for a RESEARCH master's (CAD 353.69/credit, i.e. CAD 15,916.05 per 45 credits): net tuition ≈ CAD 404.70/credit ≈ CAD 18,212 for the whole 45-credit degree ≈ CAD 9,100/yr. Plus Montreal living ≈ CAD 15,000–17,000/yr. Realistic two-year total ≈ CAD 50,000. If the option is classified NON-research the bursary is CAD 251.88/credit instead. Classification of this specific option: UNVERIFIED — confirm with esp-bourses@esp.umontreal.ca.
scholarshipName: Bourse d'exemption UdeM pour personnes étudiantes de l'international (automatic); Bourses d'exemption des droits de scolarité supplémentaires (Quebec government / Ministry agreements)
scholarships: PARTIAL BUT AUTOMATIC AND REAL. (1) Bourse d'exemption UdeM: "You do not have to apply for this bursary" — awarded automatically on admission review, "applied directly to your tuition and deducted from your invoice balance each term throughout your studies". Research master's rate CAD 353.69/credit = CAD 15,916.05 over 45 credits. Covers TUITION ONLY, not living. Condition: the student must not "already benefit from another form of tuition exemption" or external funding — so it cannot be stacked. (2) Quebec country-agreement exemptions (PEE): TUNISIA IS NOT LISTED among the signatory countries on UdeM's exemption page — do not count on it. (3) UdeM's Excellence Scholarship Programme for international students, which includes a full tuition exemption plus stipend and health insurance, is restricted to DOCTORAL, postdoctoral and short-term research students — NOT master's. (4) No teaching assistantship system comparable to the US exists at master's level. VERDICT: affordable-ish, not free. He would still need ≈ CAD 25,000/yr of living money.
languageRequirement: FRENCH. This is the programme's single biggest advantage for him — he is fluent in French, so the language barrier that blocks him elsewhere disappears, and he can write the mandatory French letter of intent natively. UdeM may require a French proficiency test (TFI/TCF/DELF) for applicants whose prior degree was not in French; a Tunisian BSc is often taught partly in French which can secure exemption. Exact test/exemption rule: UNVERIFIED.
englishTest: Not applicable — no English test required. GRE: not required (not used in Canada).
deadline: 1 MARCH 2027 for Fall 2027 entry ("Automne 2027: 1 août 2026 – 1 mars 2027"). AFTER September 2026 — open to him. A Winter 2027 entry deadline of 1 September 2026 exists but is the wrong intake.
applicationOpens: 1 AUGUST 2026 for the Fall 2027 intake — the application window is ALREADY OPEN as of today.
_verdict: BEST NON-EUROPE FIT ON LANGUAGE AND COST. French-taught, in the world capital of electroacoustic music, automatic tuition bursary cutting fees to ~CAD 9k/yr, portfolio of only 2-5 works, no live audition, deadline 1 March 2027 (well within reach), applications already open. The obstacles are that he must actually build 2-5 credible sound-creation works during 2026, must find a supervisor, and must self-fund ~CAD 25k/yr of living costs — which the brief says he cannot do. Flag as 'affordable only with a living-cost solution'.

institution: Stanford University — CCRMA (Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics), Department of Music
program: M.A. in Music, Science and Technology (MA/MST)
accreditationStatus: Accredited by WSCUC (WASC Senior College and University Commission)
durationEcts: "a two-year degree granted at the successful completion of required and elective coursework totaling at least 45 units" (Stanford quarter units). No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: Exactly quoted from CCRMA: courses "developed by faculty from the domains of art, composition, computer science, engineering, human-computer interaction, intermedia, music perception, psychoacoustics, music/audio signal processing, sound synthesis and effects, and neuroscience." CCRMA is the birthplace of FM synthesis and one of the two or three most important computer-music laboratories in the world.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; application via Stanford Department of Music graduate admissions. "All applicants to the MA/MST program are encouraged to submit project reports or published papers demonstrating their commitment to and achievements in the domains spanned by CCRMA courses." Strong programming and DSP/maths preparation is the de facto bar.
acceptsNonMusic: YES in practice — the MA/MST is explicitly a science-and-technology degree and admits engineers, computer scientists and physicists; CCRMA does not require a music degree. No exact quotation of an 'any bachelor's accepted' clause is published, so: partially UNVERIFIED. His BSc Software Engineering is a genuinely competitive background here.
portfolioSpec: "All applicants to the MA/MST program are encouraged to submit project reports or published papers demonstrating their commitment to and achievements in the domains spanned by CCRMA courses." Encouraged, not mandatory. This is a technical/research portfolio (code, DSP projects, papers, instruments, installations), not a demo of tracks. Exact file-count/length limits: UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: No live audition. CCRMA MA/MST is admitted on file. (Stanford's DMA/performance degrees differ.)
tuitionNonEU: Stanford graduate tuition is roughly USD 65,000–70,000 per year at full-time enrolment (2025-26 rate; exact 2027-28 figure UNVERIFIED — Stanford publishes tuition annually at registrar.stanford.edu). Stanford charges the same tuition to international and domestic students.
otherFees: Application fee USD 125 ("The application fee is $125 and may be paid using Visa, Mastercard cards"). Mandatory Cardinal Care health insurance ≈ USD 7,500/yr. Campus/health fees. Bay Area living costs ≈ USD 30,000–36,000/yr.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ USD 105,000–115,000 PER YEAR all-in; ≈ USD 210,000+ for the two-year degree. This is one of the most expensive routes in the entire search.
scholarshipName: None systematic. Occasional CCRMA fellowship/TA support only.
scholarships: NO RELIABLE FUNDING ROUTE — MARK UNAFFORDABLE. CCRMA states plainly: "The Music Department and CCRMA do not have regular funding to support students in the MA/MST program. However, year-to-year there is occasionally some fellowship support and/or TA positions available." There is no guaranteed package, no tuition waiver, and Stanford master's students are generally expected to self-fund. Knight-Hennessy Scholars (full funding, open to all nationalities including Tunisians, covers tuition + stipend) IS technically available for a Stanford master's — but it is one of the most competitive awards on earth (~100 places from ~10,000 applicants worldwide), deadline typically mid-October, and it requires a separate application plus admission to the degree programme. Fulbright would have been the realistic route, and the Tunisia 2027 cycle CLOSED 30 JUNE 2026. VERDICT: unaffordable for this candidate for September 2027.
englishTest: TOEFL iBT required for non-native speakers; Stanford's graduate minimum recommendation is 100 iBT (Music department may state its own). IELTS is NOT accepted by Stanford for graduate admission in most departments — verify. GRE: "GRE scores are now optional for graduate applicants at CCRMA; however those wishing to focus in particular specializations might benefit from submitting GRE scores." Exact TOEFL number for Music: UNVERIFIED.
deadline: Stanford Department of Music graduate deadline is in early-to-mid December for the following autumn (US pattern: December–January, nine months before entry). For September 2027 entry the deadline falls in DECEMBER 2026. Exact date: UNVERIFIED — check music.stanford.edu graduate admissions in autumn 2026.
applicationOpens: Stanford's graduate application typically opens in September for the following autumn. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle.
_verdict: PRESTIGE FIT, FUNDING FAILURE. CCRMA is the single best-matched institution in the world for a software engineer becoming an electronic-music technologist, and it does not require a music degree. But it explicitly does not fund its master's students, costs ~USD 210k over two years, and his one realistic funding route (Fulbright Tunisia) closed on 30 June 2026. Mark UNAFFORDABLE unless he wins Knight-Hennessy.

institution: New York University — Steinhardt School, Department of Music and Performing Arts Professions
accreditationStatus: Accredited by MSCHE (Middle States); Music programmes accredited by NASM
durationEcts: "40–45" credits; full-time or part-time; normally 2 years full-time. No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: Music technology core: digital audio signal processing, audio programming (Max/MSP, C++, Python), music information retrieval, recording and production, immersive/spatial audio, acoustics, and electronic music composition. NYU's Music and Audio Research Laboratory (MARL) sits alongside the programme. Specialisations available in music production and in DSP/research.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; "Basic competence in music theory and history is a prerequisite for all graduate degree programs in music." An entrance music-theory exam is administered, and "up to 8 points of remedial music theory and/or history coursework may be required". Portfolio required.
acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY. NYU does NOT publish an explicit statement welcoming non-music bachelors. It publishes the opposite direction: "Basic competence in music theory and history is a prerequisite for all graduate degree programs in music", enforced by an advisory entrance exam, with remedial coursework (up to 8 points, billed at full tuition) imposed on those who fail it. So a software-engineering BSc is admissible but he would very likely be loaded with paid remedial theory/history credits. Music Technology is nonetheless the most engineer-friendly of NYU's music master's degrees.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: "You are required to provide a portfolio of samples of previous professional, artistic, or academic work on music, technology, and related fields." Examples given: "school papers, scientific publications (8 pages maximum), webpages or audiovisual materials of work you have composed, performed, recorded, mixed, and/or produced." Delivery: "streamed media via a reliable service like SoundCloud or Vimeo or a portfolio website." NOTE: this spec is unusually forgiving — academic and technical work counts, so a software engineer with strong audio-code projects can satisfy it without a music CV.
auditionSpec: No live audition for M.M. Music Technology — the portfolio replaces it. (Other NYU M.M. degrees such as String Studies do require auditions.) A music-theory placement/advisory exam is taken AFTER matriculation, not as an audition.
tuitionNonEU: NYU Steinhardt graduate tuition is charged per credit; full-time graduate tuition runs approximately USD 60,000–66,000 per year for a 40-45 credit master's taken over two years (2025-26 basis). Exact per-credit rate for 2027-28: UNVERIFIED — see nyu.edu/bursar.
otherFees: Application fee USD 75 ("You will be prompted to pay a $75 application fee, payable by major credit card only"). Mandatory NYU student health insurance ≈ USD 4,000–5,000/yr. Registration and services fees. NYC living costs ≈ USD 28,000–36,000/yr.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ USD 95,000–110,000 per year all-in; ≈ USD 190,000–220,000 for the degree. Among the most expensive options found anywhere.
scholarshipName: NYU Steinhardt Graduate Scholarships and Grants (partial merit awards)
scholarships: NO ADEQUATE FUNDING ROUTE — MARK UNAFFORDABLE. Steinhardt master's scholarships are PARTIAL merit tuition awards (typically a fraction of tuition, rarely more than half), do not cover living costs, and are not guaranteed. Critical operational fact: "The scholarship deadline is March 1 and those who do not have an application submitted before then will not be considered for scholarships" — but the programme deadline is 15 January, so applying by 15 January automatically preserves scholarship consideration. There is NO teaching assistantship system that waives full tuition at master's level in Steinhardt music. Fulbright Tunisia would have been the route and its 2027 cycle closed 30 June 2026.
englishTest: NYU Steinhardt graduate minimum: TOEFL iBT 100 / IELTS 7.0 for most programmes (Steinhardt sets 100 iBT as its standard; some programmes accept lower). GRE: "Not required." Exact Music Technology score minimum: UNVERIFIED — the how-to-apply page only says "See testing requirements".
deadline: "Fall Start: January 15" — i.e. 15 JANUARY 2027 for September 2027 entry. Scholarship consideration cut-off 1 March. Both AFTER September 2026.
applicationOpens: NYU's graduate application typically opens in September for the following Fall. "NYU does not have an exact date that the application will close and recommends applicants apply immediately." UNVERIFIED for 2027 cycle.
_verdict: EXCELLENT PORTFOLIO FIT, IMPOSSIBLE PRICE. The portfolio spec explicitly accepts academic and technical work, which is the friendliest wording found for a portfolio-less software engineer, and no audition is required. But Steinhardt funds master's students only with partial merit scholarships. At ~USD 200k for the degree with no assistantship route, this is unaffordable without Fulbright — which has closed for 2027. Include as a stretch/aspiration only.

institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology — MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences (MAS)
program: S.M. in Media Arts and Sciences (via research groups: Opera of the Future / Responsive Environments / Future Sketches etc.)
accreditationStatus: Accredited by NECHE (New England Commission of Higher Education)
durationEcts: "The MAS master of science degree requires a residency of two academic years." No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: You are admitted to a specific research group and build/research inside it. The music-relevant groups are Opera of the Future (Tod Machover — hyperinstruments, opera, new interfaces, music and technology), Responsive Environments (Joseph Paradiso — sensor systems, wearable/electronic instruments, spatial audio), plus groups in generative/computational media. Output is built artefacts, instruments, systems and a thesis, not a record.
entryRequirements: "you must have completed your Bachelor's degree by the time you enroll in our Master's program." Application = Statement of Objectives, Personal Statement, Portfolio, transcripts, three recommendation letters. Admission is decided by the individual research group whose faculty member wants you; the group, not a central committee, drives the outcome.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — emphatically. MAS is not a music degree and imposes no music prerequisite; MIT's FAQ requires only "a completed Bachelor's degree" with no field restriction. The Media Lab is famous for admitting engineers, designers and self-taught builders. A BSc Software Engineering is a mainstream, competitive background here. (No explicit sentence saying 'any field' is published, so the wording is inferred from the absence of any restriction — partially UNVERIFIED.)
portfolioSpec: "Some research groups require the submission of a portfolio of relevant work, and most other groups will accept such portfolios for consideration. Applicants should consult the applicant information webpages of the research groups they are applying to for specific requirements." So there is NO single Institute-wide portfolio spec — it is set per research group. For Opera of the Future / Responsive Environments the de facto expectation is documented built work (instruments, software, installations, demo videos, code repositories), which a software engineer can assemble without any musical training. Exact per-group specs for the 2027 cycle: UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: NO AUDITION. There is no performance audition anywhere in the MAS process — this is an engineering/design school, not a conservatoire. Selection is by statement, portfolio, letters and (for shortlisted candidates) interviews with the research group.
tuitionNonEU: MIT graduate tuition ≈ USD 63,000–66,000/yr (2025-26 basis; exact 2027-28 figure UNVERIFIED) — BUT IT IS PAID FOR YOU. See scholarships.
otherFees: Application fee USD 90 ("Yes, our application fee is $90"). Medical insurance is covered by the funding package. Cambridge/Boston living costs are covered by the stipend.
totalCostEstimate: EFFECTIVELY ZERO NET COST, plus a positive stipend. The candidate would be paid to attend.
scholarshipName: MAS Research Assistantship (institutional, automatic for all admitted MAS students)
scholarships: STRONGEST FUNDING ROUTE IN THE ENTIRE NON-EUROPE SEARCH. MIT states flatly: "Media Arts and Sciences (MAS) students are fully funded including tuition, medical insurance, and a stipend" and "All MAS graduate students are currently fully supported (tuition, medical insurance, plus a stipend)." Mechanism: "All Media Lab graduate students are supported by Research Assistantships, which pays tuition and a modest stipend for living expenses." Renewal: "Funding is renewed yearly, contingent on satisfactory academic and research performance, and alignment with research priorities." CITIZENSHIP: this is an internal RA appointment, not a citizenship-restricted award — TUNISIANS ARE FULLY ELIGIBLE. No separate scholarship application exists; admission IS the funding. Covers tuition AND living. Deadline = the admission deadline (15 December).
englishTest: TOEFL or IELTS required for international applicants: "More information on the IELTS/TOEFL requirement is available on the International Students page." MIT generally prefers IELTS and its typical graduate guidance is IELTS 7.0+ / TOEFL iBT 100+. EXACT MAS minimum: UNVERIFIED. GRE: "GRE scores are not required" / "MAS does not require or use GRE scores."
deadline: 15 DECEMBER ("11:59pm ET on December 15 is the firm deadline for all applications") — i.e. 15 DECEMBER 2026 for September 2027 entry. AFTER September 2026, so still reachable. Decisions from late February.
applicationOpens: 15 SEPTEMBER ("The application opens on September 15th") — i.e. ~15 September 2026 for the 2027 intake.
_verdict: THE SINGLE BEST FUNDING ANSWER FOUND. Fully funded (tuition + insurance + stipend), no music degree required, no audition, no GRE, deadline 15 Dec 2026 — all constraints satisfied. The catch is brutal selectivity (single-digit admit rate, and you must convince one specific faculty member) and that it is a technology-research degree, not an artist degree: he would leave as a music-technology researcher/instrument-builder, not as a producer with a release. Should be his highest-effort US application.

institution: Dartmouth College — Department of Music / Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies
program: M.F.A. in Sonic Practice (successor to the former M.A. in Digital Musics)
durationEcts: Three academic years full-time; "a minimum of eleven terms fully enrolled". No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: For "Composers, artists, and scholars working expansively with sound": faculty mentorship, seminars and group critiques plus cross-disciplinary coursework in "music, computer science, theater, engineering, studio art, philosophy". Dartmouth's Bregman Media Labs are a historic electronic-music centre. The programme explicitly names "composition, sound art, music theater, instrumental performance, songwriting, improvisation, spatial audio, sound installation and/or electronic music" as its sonic-arts remit.
entryRequirements: "a bachelor's degree in a field relevant to their creative and/or scholarly practice" plus "Demonstrated knowledge and experience in some area of sonic arts".
acceptsNonMusic: YES in principle — the requirement is "a bachelor's degree in a field relevant to their creative and/or scholarly practice", not a music degree, and the curriculum deliberately draws on "engineering, visual art, computer science". BUT the second clause — "Demonstrated knowledge and experience in some area of sonic arts" — is a hard gate that a candidate with no portfolio cannot currently clear.
portfolioSpec: A creative portfolio demonstrating sonic-arts practice is required. Exact specification (number of works, duration, format): NOT PUBLISHED on the pages retrieved — UNVERIFIED. Contact Sonic.Practice@dartmouth.edu.
auditionSpec: No live audition stated; assessment is on portfolio and file. UNVERIFIED whether shortlisted candidates are interviewed.
tuitionNonEU: N/A — tuition is fully waived for admitted students. (Dartmouth graduate list tuition ≈ USD 63,000/yr; never paid by MFA students.)
otherFees: Covered — health insurance included in the package; a relocation bonus is paid.
totalCostEstimate: ZERO net cost plus a large positive stipend, IF admitted.
scholarshipName: Guarini School full funding package for the Sonic Practice MFA
scholarships: OUTSTANDING FUNDING — BUT SEE THE BLOCKER BELOW. The programme is "a three-year, fully funded graduate program. All MFA students receive full tuition waivers, health insurance, a living stipend ($47,000 in 2024–25), and a relocation bonus"; the 2025-26 stipend was USD 48,410.04. Structure: "3 fully-funded academic years (tuition coverage + work stipend)" for "20 hours of work (coursework + research) per week". The Guarini School names Sonic Practice MFA among the small set of master's programmes carrying its competitive funding package. Citizenship-blind — Tunisians eligible. Covers tuition AND living in full.
englishTest: TOEFL/IELTS required for international applicants; exact minimum NOT PUBLISHED on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED. GRE: "The Graduate Record Examination is not required for application to the program."
deadline: *** BLOCKER FOR THIS CANDIDATE *** The Guarini admissions page for Sonic Practice states: "This program is not accepting applications for the 2027-28 admissions cycle." The programme therefore has NO September 2027 intake. The most recent published deadline was 15 January 2026 (for 2026-27 entry). He would have to target the 2028-29 cycle, deadline likely ~15 January 2028.
applicationOpens: N/A for 2027-28 — cycle suspended. Historically opened in the autumn preceding a 15 January deadline.
_verdict: PERFECT PROGRAMME, WRONG YEAR. On paper this is the ideal answer — a fully funded, three-year sonic-arts MFA at an Ivy that pays ~USD 48k/yr and explicitly welcomes non-music bachelors from computer science and engineering. But Dartmouth has PAUSED admissions for 2027-28, so it cannot be applied to for his target intake. Keep it as the number-one target for a September 2028 start, and use 2026-27 to build the sonic-arts portfolio it demands.

program: M.A. in Music (concentration in Experimental Music / Composition)
whatYouStudy: Three concentrations: scholarship (ethnomusicology/musicology), EXPERIMENTAL MUSIC/COMPOSITION, and performance. Wesleyan is a historic centre of American experimental music (Alvin Lucier, Anthony Braxton lineage) with strong electronic/computer music, world music and improvisation. Assistantship duties include "supervising department facilities (e.g. archives, recording studio, instrument collection)".
entryRequirements: "an undergraduate music major or its equivalent is required of all applicants to the M.A. program". Materials: 3 letters of recommendation, transcripts, writing sample, CDs, scores, GRE upload, USD 85 non-refundable application fee.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — HARD BLOCKER. Wesleyan states explicitly: "an undergraduate music major or its equivalent is required of all applicants to the M.A. program." A BSc in Software Engineering with no conservatoire training and no portfolio does not meet this. The phrase "or its equivalent" leaves a theoretical door open for someone with a substantial demonstrated compositional body of work, but this candidate has none. RULE OUT for September 2027.
portfolioSpec: "Writing sample, CDs, scores" are listed among required materials — i.e. recordings and notated scores of the applicant's own work plus an academic writing sample. No item count or duration published — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: No universal live audition; "personal interviews and GRE scores are highly recommended but not required". Performance-concentration applicants are assessed on recordings. Composition applicants submit CDs and scores rather than auditioning.
tuitionNonEU: Wesleyan graduate tuition ≈ USD 68,000/yr list — but remitted for funded students (see below). Exact 2027-28: UNVERIFIED.
otherFees: Application fee USD 85. "Wesleyan University contributes two-thirds of the insurance fee for graduate students that receive a stipend toward a Wesleyan-offered health insurance plan" — so the student pays roughly a third of health insurance.
totalCostEstimate: Near zero if funded; ~USD 90,000/yr if unfunded.
scholarshipName: Wesleyan Graduate Teaching Assistantship / Fellowship with tuition remission
scholarships: GENUINELY FULL FUNDING, but gated behind the music-major requirement. "Most full-time PhD students and students in the two-year MA programs receive a stipend for assistantships or fellowships, with tuition remission included in the graduate student's financial package." Workload: "The basic workload is nine hours per week for the M.A." — unusually light. Duties are flexible: TA-ing, running the recording studio, teaching a class, assisting faculty research. No citizenship restriction — Tunisians eligible. Exact stipend amount: UNVERIFIED.
englishTest: "Official TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo English scores" required for applicants who are not US citizens/permanent residents from non-English-speaking countries. Notably: "There is not a minimum required test score." GRE: scores are uploaded to the application (Wesleyan code 3959, Department code 2404) but are "highly recommended but not required".
deadline: 15 JANUARY (the 2026 cycle deadline was 15 January 2026) — so ~15 JANUARY 2027 for September 2027 entry. AFTER September 2026. Exact 2027 date: UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: Autumn preceding the January deadline — UNVERIFIED exact date.
_verdict: FUNDED BUT INELIGIBLE. One of the very few genuinely funded US music master's degrees (tuition remission + stipend for only 9 hrs/week), and no minimum English test score — but the explicit requirement of "an undergraduate music major or its equivalent" excludes this candidate as he currently stands. Only worth revisiting after several years of serious compositional output.

program: Ph.D. in Music and Multimedia Composition (MEME — Multimedia and Electronic Music Experiments). NOTE: the standalone MA in MEME no longer exists; a master's is awarded en route inside the PhD.
durationEcts: Funded for 6 years. Master's degree conferred en route. No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: MEME is "an interdisciplinary program within the Brown University Music Department that focuses on the creative use of emerging technology for real-time interactive performance and installation." Live electronics, computer music, multimedia composition, instrument building, installation. Facilities: the MEME studios and the Granoff Center for the Creative Arts — "recording studios, electronics shops, project studios, exhibition and performance spaces".
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (US PhDs admit directly from a bachelor's — no master's required). Portfolio of creative work, statement, transcripts, letters.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY / UNVERIFIED as an explicit written clause. Brown does not publish a music-degree requirement for MEME, and the field routinely admits engineers and self-taught electronic musicians. The decisive gate is the creative portfolio, not the bachelor's subject. However, a candidate with literally no portfolio cannot be admitted — the four-work portfolio is mandatory.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: "an online portfolio of four examples of creative work, which can include music, videos, installations, performances, scores, or other forms of creative work, with brief notes about each work." Four works, any medium, each annotated.
auditionSpec: No live audition. Portfolio-based, with interviews for shortlisted candidates (UNVERIFIED).
tuitionNonEU: N/A — fully waived. Brown graduate list tuition ≈ USD 70,000/yr, never paid by funded PhD students.
otherFees: Health insurance covered. Application fee ≈ USD 75 (UNVERIFIED for 2027 cycle); fee waivers available.
totalCostEstimate: ZERO net cost plus a stipend for six years.
scholarshipName: Brown University Graduate School full PhD funding package (fellowships + teaching assistantships)
scholarships: FULL FUNDING, CITIZENSHIP-BLIND. "Successful applicants to the Ph.D. program receive full funding for 6 years, including costs for tuition and health insurance, stipend during summer months, as well as stipends for fellowships or teaching assistantships." Covers tuition AND living AND summers. Tunisians eligible — Brown's PhD funding is internal and not restricted by nationality. No separate scholarship application; admission carries the funding. Exact stipend: UNVERIFIED (Brown's humanities PhD stipend is in the ~USD 40,000+/yr range).
englishTest: TOEFL/IELTS required of international applicants; Brown Graduate School standard is TOEFL iBT ~100 / IELTS 7.0. Exact Music department minimum: UNVERIFIED. GRE: not required (Brown Music dropped GRE) — UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle.
deadline: US pattern, early-to-mid December or early January for the following September. For September 2027 entry expect DECEMBER 2026 – JANUARY 2027. Exact date: UNVERIFIED — check music.brown.edu/graduate in autumn 2026.
_verdict: A REAL FUNDING ROUTE, BUT IT IS A DOCTORATE, NOT A MASTER'S. Six years fully funded with tuition, insurance and summer stipend, no music degree required in writing, and only four portfolio works needed — that is the lowest portfolio bar of any fully funded US programme found. The mismatch is that he wants to become a working electronic-music artist, and this is a six-year academic commitment producing a scholar-composer. Include as a serious fallback if he is willing to commit to a PhD. He must have four credible works by December 2026.
